title: Security tool tampering
overview: Review a defensive tool state change and determine whether it is supported by a change record.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: An unexpected stopped state for an endpoint protection service warrants checking management heartbeat and actor.
evidence: Check the service, new state, surrounding activity, managed heartbeat and any maintenance authorization.
false_positive: An approved upgrade can temporarily stop an agent.
tuning: Treat the maintenance window as expiring context, and check for restart and protection recovery.
response: Preserve logs, verify endpoint health from a separate source and restore protection through approved administration.
prevention: Enable tamper protection and retain service and security logs off the endpoint.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture records a state transition. It does not exercise tamper behavior or prove deliberate defense impairment.

questions.explanation: An independent health source helps verify the service outage and eventual recovery.

questions.prompt: When should a maintenance exception expire?
options: Whenever the first alert is closed
questions.explanation: An expiring exception keeps visibility of unexpected outages.
